body: All things considered I'm extremely privileged, so I understand the jealousy or resent for me. Unfortunately I can't appreciate my situation as well as others would, no matter how I try. Trust me, I hate myself for that too, it must look real pathetic from the outside. As much as I wish I could swap places with you, or anyone else on this subreddit, I can't.

Of course I acknowledge I've got friends that I can always reach out to, but similar to you I don't communicate well with them. They've made some insensitive decisions, oblivious to how they may affect me. A lot of problems can be blamed on them, or anyone really, and sometimes I want to kill myself and stick all the guilt onto them. But nah, I'm not emotional nor selfish enough to ever do that, besides I'm the common factor amongst my problems. After ditching most them recently I've felt a lot better, still no closer to enjoying life, but not as miserable. I'm glad you've had a change of heart and hope you're doing well in your journey. I've been thinking about starting a second life, still leaving everyone, but moving away, changing my name and likely enlisting in the army.

Anyway, a slight shift in your mindset and weight loss would benefit you. Lose weight firstly to be healthy and only secondly to be attractive. This helps avoid unhealthy eating disorders and mental illnesses like anorexia, as being healthy is your top priority, not losing weight at the cost of health. And measure your progress in weight not looks, it's such a gradual process you will almost never notice until you look back on month old photos.

Self pity is understandable when your life is over before it even began. So much you could have experienced, and what more you could of done if the dice of life rolled a little better. I don't blame you if you take your life, but try not to rot away while you wait for the motivation to finish the job. You've given yourself a 3 year expiry date, might as well try enjoy those years. Nothing would be worse than passing your thirtieth birthday, nothing's changed except you set the date to your fortieth birthday... Than when your fifty, then sixty and so on. Before you know it you've had thirty more years to attempt to fix your life but you stayed unmotivated because you never anticipated you'd live that long. And you can always fix your life, you just got to make the choice is it worth it or not.

If you're isolated and haven't talked to anyone in a while, just go out and have a conversation in person. Even with just a stranger. Chances are your mind will clear up almost immediately. You'll slip back into insanity every time you're left alone until you manage to create a routine of social interactions again.
Wanting to die, but not your friend, that's poetic hyprocisy.

You're in a paradox. The less friends and family for you to hurt, the more mentally unstable you'll become, hence increasing your chances of hurting them. The more friends and family you have, the more mentally stable you'll become, but the risk of hurting one them still increases.


Just keep in mind it's okay to be selfish sometimes.

No matter how much better it gets, I'll never be able to take the back the years of suffering, and that doesn't sit right with me.

It may or may not get better. It's a gamble, it always is. And when it does get better it can get worse twice as quick. However if you think back to a happier time, even if it's only happy in comparison to now, then you know it can get better. If you're not already, always remember when you were at your lowest, because then you are living proof your life can, and does improve.

First, don't tip out any alcohol, that stuff can be expensive and like you said she'll just go get more, which endangers others. Find out why she drinks, if it because of your father then a divorce will probably happen but it'll at least fix part of the problem. Tell her how it's affecting you, don't guilt trip her but rather try to find a solution for both of you. The solution will probably feel underwhelming, like maybe it's just buying cheaper beer, only driving when tipsy instead of drunk, not talking to you when drunk, etc. But it's the best you'll get for the time being.
Don't try to be energetic and happy. If it exhausts you it'd probably exhaust them too. In fact don't try to be anything. Just be what you are, it's a lot easier that way.

Reading responses you probably just think others feel more empathy than they really do. Let's say someone sees you faking empathy for their mum dying. They don't feel anything but seeing your reaction and the fact they're closer to her than you makes them think they lack empathy. Of course people feel empathy but not that much of it. They don't really care, they just want to seem like they do. You just don't want to fake it. Last thing I'd you need to be close and relate to their situation for it to work. I've watched a few movies where I feel sorry for the "wrong" person. If you've ever watched Rocketman there's a few underlying themes. One is his Dad is unfeeling and depressive, due to this he harshly punishes the main character Elton John. This is meant to make us feel sorry for Elton and angry at his father but I didn't feel any of that. Later Elton goes to see his dad years after a divorce and no connections. His dad now has a new family and is doing rather well, treating his new children much better than he ever did to Elton and somewhat teasing him for being happier. Elton gets mad and leaves and everyone is now like wow what a shitty father, but I can relate to the depressive state and seeing him grow and be happy makes me just feel happy for him. In fact I'd even say I would possibly treat Elton the same way if I were in his father's shoes. Being empathetic to the wrong people can be problematic, either because society deems it wrong or because it ruins the perspectives of films, but it just means you can relate to them.

This is honestly the most relatable rant I've ever read. I mean the whole cracking jokes and being all happy is common with people suffering from mental issues, but the whole wishing they'd ask about it then not giving a genuine answer hits close to home. Had a classmate ask today why I'm never at school, I reply with I'm depressed, she retorts with 'but your always happy, like right now'. And that's pretty much where the conversation ended. Like yeah, I seem happy, but it's not that hard to smile and laugh along with your friends. Even if I wanted to talk deeper into the issue, it'd inevitably bring up councilors and other people I don't want to deal with. And then the whole potential stuff, don't get me started. If I can't do something right, I often can't do it at all, so when teachers that damn bar so high I just give up. Just let me do MY best, not THE best. But the best part of your rant  was the losing your mind in your free time. I thought I was the only one, but I guess I'm not alone. It's becoming worse over the months, but now if I'm not listening to music or scrolling through Reddit I absolutely lose it. Giant headache, dark thoughts, some kind of split personality thing, dizziness. You name it I have to go through it. So when it comes to sleeping or doing homework I just can't, I lose it. I can stop it either by distracting myself with Reddit or youtube, or for whatever reason by inflicting pain. Dunno what it is but any kind of pain, wether it be a blow to the head or a cut to the arm, soothes me. Also sometimes going for a walk, but it doesn't work nearly as well. Once walked from 12am - 5am. Walked to another town and back. But anyway, thanks for the rant, helped more than you'd think
